Find and set the tempo

Tap the display in time with the music. After a few taps it shows the BPM, the gap between taps (Interval) and how even your taps are (Steady).

Drag the display up or down to set a tempo (the ▲ ▼ beside the BPM are the reminder). Drag on the big whole number to move 1 BPM at a time, or on the decimal to move 0.1.

÷2 and ×2 halve or double the tempo, for when you counted twice as fast or slow as you meant to.

Reset (↻) clears the taps and stops the click.

The click

Click starts and stops the metronome. Its dot lights while it runs.

Flash flashes the display on every beat, brightest on beat 1. Handy on a loud stage or with headphones off.

Click volume sets how loud the click is. If you hear nothing, check the ring/silent switch: the click follows it.

Time, Sub, Sound and Train

Tap any of the four to change it.

Time is the time signature. Pick one, or make your own: set the beats per bar and note value, an optional grouping like 2+2+3, and tap beats to choose which are accented.

Sub adds subdivisions between beats: 8ths, triplets or 16ths.

Sound picks the click: beep, woodblock, rimshot, cowbell, hi-hat, kick or snare.

Train helps you practice. Ramp changes the tempo by a set amount every few bars until it reaches a target. Gaps plays some bars and goes silent for others, so you keep time on your own. Random drops beats at random.

Analyze a song

Audio file finds the BPM of a song on your phone. Record listens through the mic while you play the song out loud.

Record starts with a count-in: one bar of clicks at the metronome tempo. Recording starts on the next beat 1, and the click stops so the mic hears only you. Tap Record during the count-in to cancel.

Search a song finds a song's BPM by name. With Apple Music, the song plays right in Betternome.

Under the BPM, Confidence says how sure the analysis is, Drift how much the tempo wanders, and Length how long the song is.

Play + click plays the song with the metronome on top. Under it, the slider and ↺10 / 10↻ move through the song; while stopped, they set where Play starts.

Pick the pulse offers half, double and other feels of the same tempo, if the song feels different to you.

Tempo over time charts the tempo across the song, so you can see where it speeds up or slows down.

Loop a section

While the song plays, tap IN on beat 1 of the section, then OUT where it ends. Or tap IN and pick a length under Bars.

OUT always lands on a whole number of bars, so the click stays in time on every pass.

Drag the IN or OUT time sideways to move it a beat at a time.

Loop turns the loop on and off. Clear removes it.

Metronome click chooses whether the click plays along (Click on) or you hear just the song (Song only). While a song plays, the Click key does the same: it turns the click on or off and the song keeps playing.

Song speed

Original plays the song as recorded, and the metronome follows the song.

Follow metronome lets you slow the song down or speed it up: tap or drag the display and the song follows, from half to double speed.

Keep pitch changes the speed without changing the key. Tape speed works like a tape machine: faster sounds higher, slower sounds lower.

Song speed works with audio files. Apple Music and Spotify songs play at their own speed.

Apple Music and Spotify

Apple Music: tap Connect Apple Music, search, pick a song and tap Play. Playing songs needs an Apple Music subscription; search still finds the BPM without one.

Under PLAY, ↺10 and 10↻ jump back or forward 10 seconds, and the slider moves anywhere in the song.

Spotify: tap Connect Spotify, then Use what's playing to pick up the song playing in Spotify. Play / pause needs Spotify Premium.

Loops work with both. Apple doesn't let apps hear the song, so the click counts from your IN tap and stays in step as the song plays.

Tap the beat (Apple Music): if the click sits off the beat, tap along with the song a few times and the click lines up with your taps. If your taps keep a different tempo than the one on file, it offers to use yours.

No BPM on file for a song? The click plays at the metronome tempo. Tap Tap the beat along with the song and it offers the tempo you tapped.

Click timing fine-tunes the click by ear, for headphones or speakers that add a delay. Spotify can only jump, so its loop can land a fraction of a second early or late; use Click timing there too.

Setlists

Tap ☰ to open Setlists. Set the tempo, time, sub, sound and trainer for a song, type its name and tap Save current.

A setlist song doesn't need audio: with no song loaded, it saves just the metronome settings. Good for live sets and practice.

With a song loaded, it's saved too, with its loop, so you can pick up where you left off. Turn off Save with “song” to save just the metronome settings.

The song you're on shows under the display. Use ‹ › to move to the previous or next song. Songs don't advance on their own.

Free has one setlist of up to 5 songs. With Pro, keep as many setlists as you like, as long as you like.

Color

The dots at the bottom of the screen change the accent color: teal, orange, lime or hot pink. Teal is free; the others come with Pro.

Betternome Pro

Betternome is free. Pro is one payment, no subscription, and adds loops, song speed, the Ramp, Gaps and Random trainers, unlimited setlists and all colors.

Every Pro feature works once for free, so you can try it first.

Tap, drag, the click, Flash, Sub, sounds, time signatures, Analyze, and Apple Music and Spotify search are always free.

Got a new phone? Tap ? and then Restore purchase. Pro comes back free on any iPhone with your Apple Account.
